_note: Spoken/captioned lines of job solstice (21-22 Dec). Text only today (Lykta say()); feed to the voice pipeline / recording studio later. who: lykta, gammel (Gammel-Rod), mor (Mor Bla), pelle, npc (lost neighbours/neighbours), aasland (radio), vik.

lines.text: The dark is climbing the valley. Fifteen small fires, remember. Light what you can. Bowlinghallen stays warm if you need to catch your breath.
This is the long one. Every fire you light pushes the night back. I do not know how far. Nobody has ever checked.
The cold from the crater just took every fire you ever lit. Rude. They remember how to burn. I put all fifteen on your map. Go, go, go.
One. The night just took a small step back. Listen: it is annoyed.
Four. Somewhere up in the passes the nisse have started singing. Badly. Beautifully.
Eight. Halfway. The Hollows are hesitating. I have never seen a Hollow hesitate.
Twelve. The grey thing at the edge of town is leaning away from the light. Three more.
One more. Whichever one is nearest. Run. Walk fast. Do something with legs.
That is all fifteen, but the mountain did not answer. It does not want an afternoon. I think it wants the dark.
Fifteen burning in daylight. The mountain is polite. It is waiting. Hold on to that feeling, and your lantern.
Look east. Past the Liland road. Something very big just opened one eye. A warm one. I did not know it could be warm.
And the grey one is turning. It is not angry. It just has somewhere else to be. Everybody pretend you are not relieved. I will go first. ...I am relieved.
Dawn. So close. Thirteen, fourteen, I stopped counting out of nerves. The grey went home anyway. I think it got bored of us. That is a win.
Dawn. Not every fire took, and the dark came a bit too far in. We are still here, though. Slightly singed, slightly proud. Warm is warm.
Dawn. It was a very long night and there were very few fires. Do not apologise to me. Apologise to the stairs you ran up. We are still here.
Gammel-Rød: Nobody gets past the Hat Brigade tonight. Not the Hush, not the Hollows, not Mor Blå's gossip.
Mor Blå: I knitted these lantern covers warm. They hold. Whatever comes, it comes round us.
Gammel-Rød: Red hats left, blue hats right. Do not tell Mor Blå I said she was right about the spacing.
Mor Blå: Fifteen fires, sweetheart. Count them. It is the only thing the dark cannot do.
Pelle (in the mask): It counts us. Tonight it is counting the fires instead. Please keep it busy.
A kid in a panda mask is standing with the nisse. He says his name is Pelle. He says he is not scared. His knees are doing a different thing.
Morning. The lights are back on. Some of them look... embarrassed. Check on someone. Anyone. Warm is a team sport.
Grey people are standing about the square, looking up. Hold the lantern up and talk to them gently. They are not angry. They are lost.
You need the lantern for this. Light is the only thing that wakes them gently. I would offer myself but I am being held at the moment.
Where am I? ...Is it Thursday? Why am I holding a ladle?
Oh no. Did I miss Christmas? ...No. I can smell cinnamon. I did not.
I was somewhere very grey. There was a queue. Everyone was facing the same way. It was not a good queue.
Thank you. I walked a long way, slowly, toward a light that was not there. It is lovely to be wrong.
Is that a lantern? Is the lantern talking? ...Hello, lantern.
Hello. Do not tell anyone I was holding my breath.
It came back on. Look at it. It is trying very hard to look as if it never left.
Oh! You came. The lights went out and I stood in the hall for an hour holding a spoon. I have no idea why the spoon.
I am fine. I am absolutely fine. Would you like a waffle? I am going to make fourteen waffles.
Something sat on the roof all night and sighed. I made it tea. It did not drink the tea, but the tea is gone.
My fairy lights are back. They look... embarrassed. Mine especially.
I had a candle, then another candle, then the whole street had candles. It was rather lovely, actually.
Something small and red just stepped out from behind the bins and went in. A house nisse. They are coming home.
Aasland (radio): All units. The case is closed.
Vik: Closed? Director, there was a thing. A big grey thing. I watched it eat a lamp.
Aasland (radio): Official finding. Weather, and a large rock. The nisser were called, not taken. The witch was a misunderstanding. The lights are the council's fault.
Vik: And the fifteen fires on the hills?
Aasland (radio): Bonfire season. Excellent turnout. Case closed. I will stamp it twice.
Vik (to you, lowering the radio): Between us, I think she knows. She just hates paperwork that argues back.
Case closed. I have never been so happy to be filed under "weather".
Three small red shapes are crossing the square toward the tape. Nobody wrote that down. Vik wrote it down, and then crossed it out.
